newsitem.title: UK: HORSE RACING-PENPIX OF LEADING GUINEAS FANCIES AT NEWMARKET.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-PENPIX OF LEADING GUINEAS FANCIES AT NEWMARKET.

text.p: Following are penpix of leading contenders in the English 2,000 and 1,000 Guineas run at Newmarket this weekend:
2,000 Guineas (for three-year-old colts and fillies, run over 1.6 km on Saturday. Starts 1440GMT)
Best two-year-old of 1996 when unbeaten in four races, including two group ones. Beaten on seasonal debut at Newbury last month, but not fully ready and expected to do much better now.

Only raced once in his career, winning at Royal Ascot last June, but is already favourite for the Epsom Derby and is fancied in some quarters to emulate Nashwan who won the Guineas en route to capturing the Derby in 1989.
Another lightly raced colt (one race, one win), but represents the Godolphin operation of Sheikh Mohammed which won the race 12 months ago with Mark of Esteem.

Very impressive winner of a Guineas trial race at Newmarket last month and looks sure to go close if reproducing that form although faces a stiffer task this time. Trainer thinks the horse represents his best chance of winning the Guineas since he sent out Mill Reef in 1971.
Two wins from two races as a juvenile, not seen out since end of July but backed in last few days from 12-1. Jockey in very good form and combination holds good each-way prospects.
Thought to have the potential to become another top class miler for trainer Cumani but may need a little more time to reach his peak. Has the assistance of champion jockey on board. - - - -
1,000 Guineas (for three-year-old fillies, run over 1.6 km on Sunday; starts 1445GMT)
Trainer has won the race three times in her career and Pas de Reponse has the form to make it four. Said to have done an excellent gallop at Chantilly on Monday.

Favourite for the Guineas until running a disappointing fourth in her preparatory race at Newbury two weeks ago. However, was boxed in that day and expected to do much better on Sunday. Has been sparkling on the gallops.
Runs for the Godophin team which has to be respected at every level, especially in the classics. Second behind Pas de Reponse in the Cheveley Park Stakes -- a useful classic guide.

The second of Henry Cecil's three-strong raiding party. Without the benefit of a race this season, but did a trial at Newbury racecourse last weekend with stable companion Reams of Verse (9-1). Trainer and jockey both big-time players. Cecil won Guineas last year with Bosra Sham.
